Key Health Benefits of Ragi Flour Rich Source of Calcium: Ragi is an excellent, non-dairy source of calcium, crucial for building and maintaining strong bones and teeth, particularly for children and older adults. Supports Weight Loss: Due to high dietary fiber and protein, consuming ragi helps maintain a feeling of fullness for longer, which reduces cravings and calorie intake. Manages Diabetes: With a low glycemic index, ragi helps regulate blood sugar levels, making it ideal for managing diabetes. High Iron Content: Ragi is rich in iron, which helps in treating or preventing anemia, increasing hemoglobin levels. Gluten-Free & Rich in Nutrients: It is a suitable alternative for those with gluten allergies and is packed with essential amino acids, B-complex vitamins, and antioxidants. Improves Digestion & Heart Health: The fiber content helps prevent constipation, while its antioxidant properties and magnesium content help lower "bad" cholesterol and promote heart health. Boosts Lactation: Regular intake of ragi is believed to improve milk production in nursing mothers. #supneelkaur #roti #ragi #europe #healthyliving

Day 54/70: High-protein Ragi Porridge👇 Ingredients: 	•	2 tbsp Ragi flour 	•	Water (to mix + cook) 	•	Milk (any of your choice) 	•	Monk fruit sweetener 	•	Cardamom seeds (or powder) 	•	Vanilla protein powder (optional, but 👌) 	•	Chia seeds & chopped nuts How to: 	1.	Mix ragi flour with water (no lumps!) 	2.	Add to pan on medium-low heat, keep stirring 	3.	Blend cardamom + sweetener and stir into the mix 	4.	Add milk once it thickens 	5.	Let it cool a bit and add protein powder 	6.	Top with chia seeds and nuts

You can try traditional Latvian food like 🫛🥓 grey peas with bacon, 🥟 piragi and 🍪 gingerbread, along with steaming cups of mulled wine and Riga Black Balsam. 🎶 There are also live performances, traditional Latvian folk music, carol singing and dancing throughout the festive season.
